before.text: **The received version.** "Kodak missed digital" is among the most repeated business anecdotes of the last twenty years, and it is factually inverted. Kodak invented digital photography in 1975 and shelved it. Kodak invented the Bayer filter in 1976 and licensed it out to everyone while protecting film. Every photograph taken today descends from Kodak twice, through the sensor and through the habit.

before.name: the outline
before.label: before the essay
before.text: Kodak invented digital photography in 1975 and shelved it. The next year it patented the color filter that sits inside nearly every digital image sensor ever manufactured, and licensed it to the entire industry while protecting its film business. The company did not miss the future. It built the future and chose to collect rent on it rather than compete with itself. Every photograph taken today descends from Kodak twice over, through that patent and through the habit of taking pictures at all.

before.passage: Kodak invented digital photography in 1975 and shelved it. The next year one of its own engineers patented the color filter array that lets a sensor see in color, and Kodak licensed it out to the industry while protecting its film business. That patent expired in July 1993, fourteen years before the iPhone, and the invention became free to anyone who wanted it. The company did not miss the future. It built the future and chose to collect rent on it until the rent ran out.
